origin.description: Third cumulant of one vector, or a third-order product moment of three vectors.
origin.usage: cum3(a, b = a, c = a, unbiased = TRUE)

arguments.name: b
arguments.text: A second vector of the same length. The default is a.

arguments.name: c
arguments.text: A third vector of the same length. The default is a.

arguments.name: unbiased
arguments.text: If true, use the unbiased multiplier n/((n-1)*(n-2)). If false, use 1/n.

origin.details: The multiplier is applied to sum((a - mean(a)) * (b - mean(b)) * (c - mean(c))). Each mean is taken on that vector before the product is formed. A shorter vector is recycled.
origin.example:
a <- c(1, 2, 4, 7, 11)
cum3(a)
cum3(a, unbiased = FALSE)
cum3(a, c(1, 3, 2, 5, 8))

translation.description: Third cumulant of one vector, or a third-order product moment of three vectors.

arguments.name: a
arguments.text: A vector of observations. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: b
arguments.text: A second vector. None uses a.

arguments.name: c
arguments.text: A third vector. None uses a.

arguments.name: unbiased
arguments.text: If true, use the unbiased multiplier n/((n-1)*(n-2)). If false, use 1/n.

translation.details: The multiplier is applied to sum((a - mean(a)) * (b - mean(b)) * (c - mean(c))). Each mean is taken on that vector before the product is formed. A shorter vector is recycled, and a length that does not divide the longer one warns.
translation.example:
from boot.util import cum3

a = [1, 2, 4, 7, 11]
print(cum3(a))
print(cum3(a, unbiased=False))
print(cum3(a, [1, 3, 2, 5, 8]))
